children: OTTAWA--Canada's nonfarm payrolls edged upward in September after two consecutive months of decline. The job-vacancy rate also rose for the first time since December.

Statistics Canada said Thursday its payroll-employment survey indicated a 9,700 gain in September, or a 0.1% increase. On a 12-month basis, nonfarm payrolls rose 0.7%, or by 127,800. The jump in September failed to reverse the 31,400 jobs shed in July and August.

Canada's nonfarm payrolls report is released on a lagged basis compared to the more closely watched and timelier labor-force survey. The labor-force survey indicated Canada lost roughly 68,000 jobs in September.

Canada's labor market has hit a rough patch, with the unemployment rate climbing to 6.7% in October from 6.5% in the previous month. Some economists had argued the weak jobs data could persuade the Bank of Canada from delivering a second straight rate hike in December. But remarks this week from Gov. Tiff Macklem have economists predicting another quarter-point rate increase on Dec. 9, to 2.75%, with central bank officials increasingly worried about a prolonged period of upward price pressure.

Statistics Canada said job vacancies in September rose 3.4% from August, marking the first increase in nine months. The job-vacancy rate, or the ratio of vacant positions as a share of labor demand, climbed to 2.9% in September after nine straight months at 2.8%.
The payroll report added average weekly earnings rose 3.3% in September.
